alternative_hypothesis: The lagged BAA10Y change (basis points, latest available at the decision close) has a positive coefficient in the daily BAA10Y->VXN partial lead-lag regression (spread widening predicts higher next-day VXN log changes), with partial R-squared at least 0.005 and a positive holdout out-of-sample incremental R-squared. Note on wording: the planner draft's 'positive, out-of-sample component' refers to positive incremental explanatory power (incremental R-squared above zero), not to a positive coefficient — the expected coefficient sign is positive on the economic argument in the mechanism, independently of that wording.
benchmark: Own-history baseline: next-day VXN log change predicted from its own lagged log change and the SPX common-factor control only, without the lagged BAA10Y change
cost_assumptions: VXN is a volatility index and is not tradable; VXN futures (VN) existed historically on CFE (CFTC-certified 2012-05-08, listed through at least 2019) but are not in CFE's current product list (the March 2026 expiration circular lists no VN; broker specification pages list only VX/VXM/VXT for CFE volatility), and no free VXN futures price series exists to measure roll costs: Yahoo VN=F returns no data (verified 2026-11-19 — HTTP 404)
The cost gate is therefore informational, not a verdict criterion; the holdout out-of-sample incremental R-squared carries the economic weight
The reported gross sign-rule edge applies no costs at all and is an upper bound on any tradable edge
cost_model: Informational only (study 003's precedent for a volatility-index target): VXN is not tradable; VXN futures (VN) existed historically on CFE but are not in CFE's current product list, and no free VXN futures price series exists to measure roll costs (Yahoo VN=F returns no data — verified 2026-11-19, HTTP 404). The trial reports the gross sign-rule edge on holdout out-of-sample augmented forecasts (1x, always invested while positioned, no costs applied) as an informational upper bound on any tradable edge, with a block-bootstrap confidence interval; the holdout out-of-sample incremental R-squared carries the economic weight. The cost gate is not a verdict criterion.
design_note: Researcher decisions beyond the planner draft (rank 1, credit-baa-10y-spread__index-vxn): (1) the predictor is the daily LEVEL change of the spread in basis points, not the log return the draft's target_definition names — a spread quoted in percentage points has no meaningful log return (same correction as studies 008/009/010); the target's log change is correct as drafted, since VXN is an index level; (2) the universe adds index:sp500 as the common-factor control leg — the draft's research question assumes a common-factor control but names none, and the lab convention (studies 001/003/008/010) is a third-asset control in the primary test; lagged VIX is deliberately NOT the control: VIX and VXN are highly correlated equity-volatility indices, so a VIX control would absorb the common volatility factor the hypothesis is about and make the test overly conservative; TYVIX is unsuitable because it ends in 2020 and would truncate the sample; lagged SPX returns are the natural equity common factor, and study 003 used SPX as its factor with predictor-day alignment; (3) the control uses control_lag_steps=0 (the SPX log change over day t, SPX[t]): Yahoo posts the close the same evening, so it is knowable at the decision close — per the study-007 publication-lag module, Yahoo market data carries no posting lag and is not shifted; (4) the BAA10Y predictor is lagged 2 trading days by availability (see the publication-lag note in the README), so the effective predictor for the log change over t+1 is the change ending at t-2 — this is a lag-2 predictor by value date, deliberately, and the report says so; (5) the cost gate is informational, not a verdict criterion, following study 003's precedent for a volatility-index target — the verdict therefore has three criteria, not four. Note on the futures check: the brief for this study assumed VXN futures do not exist; verification showed they did exist (CFE, symbol VN, CFTC-certified 2012-05-08, listed through at least 2019) but are not in CFE's current product list, and no free price series exists (Yahoo VN=F, HTTP 404, verified 2026-11-19) — the informational treatment stands, on the corrected facts; (6) the sample is the full window (2003-01-02 to the fetch date): VXN is still published, and this is the first study to use the refreshed VXN panel (PR #25, VXNCLS to 2026-11-17) — the windows follow study 008/010 (train to 2020, validation to 2024, holdout 2024 to the fetch date).
exclusions: Bars outside the sample window (2003-01-02 to 2026-11-19) are out of sample; the panel ends where the data ends (the FRED legs bind, one trading day behind the fetch date).
Incomplete synchronized rows are excluded and counted.
FRED empty-field missing values are excluded at fetch time and counted.
The first two panel return rows have no lagged BAA10Y change and are dropped.
The naive unlagged alignment, the no-factor control, the reverse placebo and the sub-period stability split are descriptive only and are not in the test family.
known_confounders: BAA10Y is defined as the BAA yield minus the 10-year Treasury yield (DGS10); the spread change nets out the rates level by construction, so a common rates shock moves both legs and is differenced out — the predictor measures the credit-specific component. The DGS10 leg is therefore not a separate control.

VXN is itself an equity-volatility measure, so the equity channel is partly the mechanism under test rather than a confounder to control: an equity shock that moves both the spread and equity volatility is the transmission the hypothesis describes, not a bias to remove. The SPX control absorbs the day-t equity move itself, not the volatility channel. Lagged VIX is deliberately not a control: VIX and VXN are highly correlated equity-volatility indices, so a VIX control would absorb the common volatility factor and make the test overly conservative.

The 2-trading-day BAA10Y availability lag is verified behaviorally (6b evidence probe 2026-11-18T21:45Z plus the fetch-time re-check) and assumed constant across the sample. If the historical posting lag differed, the predictor alignment is wrong for those periods.
FRED series are revised over time; the fetch records the current vintage. Historical values as first published may differ from the current vintage (revision risk is unmodelled).

The own-history baseline uses the VXN log change over day t as a predictor for the change over t+1. Under the study's source-based PIT convention (FRED posts day-t values the next business day), the day-t VXN value is published the next morning, so the baseline uses information the FRED source had not yet published at the decision close. The same convention was used in studies 003, 009 and 010. It strengthens the baseline against the source, so the incremental test is conservative: the source must beat a baseline that already knows the target's most recent change.

The SPX control is the log change over day t (SPX[t], study 003's factor-alignment precedent): Yahoo posts the close the same evening, so it is knowable at the decision close. It absorbs the day-t common equity shock by design — that is what a same-day control is for.
The sample covers the 2008 crisis, the 2020 COVID crash and the 2022 rate shock; transmission may be regime-dependent. Sub-period stability is descriptive only.

VXN log changes are close to unpredictable (study 003's base-model R-squared for next-day VIX log changes was about 0.012); the baseline explains little, so the incremental R-squared is measured against a weak baseline.

The PIT store records available_at equal to the event time (adapter limitation); the publication lag is enforced in the trial's panel construction via the study-007 lagged-changes module, not in the stored observations.

This is the first study to use the refreshed VXN panel (PR #25): the VXNCLS series was re-pulled in full to 2026-11-17, and the overlap with study 003's window was verified at the aggregate level only (row and missing counts match; a count-preserving value revision cannot be excluded — see research/planner-6a/vxn_refresh.json).
mechanism: A widening BAA credit spread reflects rising credit risk premia and tightening financial conditions: corporate funding costs rise relative to Treasuries as default risk is repriced. Stress in credit markets typically coincides with rising equity volatility, as the same risk-off impulse drives deleveraging and flight-to-quality flows, and as falling equity prices mechanically raise leverage and hence volatility (the leverage effect). The Nasdaq-100 is growth- and technology-heavy, so its volatility may be at least as sensitive to credit conditions as broad-market volatility. The spread is an end-of-day published signal, so any transmission should appear the next trading day. The expected sign is positive: spread widening predicts higher next-day VXN log changes.
missing_data_policy: No forward filling; drop incomplete synchronized rows and report the dropped count. FRED empty-field missing values are excluded at fetch time and counted.
model_definition: Partial lead-lag OLS with Newey-West HAC standard errors (daily lagged BAA10Y change -> next-day VXN log change)
Purged walk-forward out-of-sample evaluation of the primary model (baseline: own history plus SPX control; augmented: plus lagged BAA10Y change)
Naive lead-lag scan (lags 0-5, raw Pearson correlations) as a descriptive upper bound (not in the test family)
Descriptive only: unlagged (naive) alignment, no-factor upper-bound control, reverse placebo (VXN->BAA10Y), sub-period stability

Cost gate is informational only (study 003's precedent): the gross sign-rule edge on holdout out-of-sample augmented forecasts, no costs applied, with a block-bootstrap confidence interval — not a verdict criterion
multiple_testing_family: Credit-spread transmission to equity volatility (1 test: daily lagged BAA10Y change -> next-day VXN log change)
null_hypothesis: Lagged BAA10Y changes have no incremental predictive value for next-day VXN log changes over VXN's own history and the SPX common-factor control, with dependence controls.
primary_metric: Partial R-squared of the lagged BAA10Y change (bp, latest available at the decision close) in the daily BAA10Y->VXN partial lead-lag regression
purge_gap_note: The purge gap equals the horizon (the minimum the validator allows). Raise it if the design needs a longer embargo; never lower it.
rejection_criteria: Holm-adjusted primary p-value at or above 0.05
Holdout out-of-sample incremental R-squared at or below 0
research_question: Does the most recent BAA10Y credit-spread change available at the close predict the next-day VXN log change beyond VXN's own history and the SPX common-factor control?
target_definition: Next-day VXN log change (FRED VXNCLS, CBOE Nasdaq-100 Volatility Index); the predictor is the most recent BAA10Y level change in basis points available at the decision close — under the verified 2-trading-day BAA10Y posting lag, the change ending two trading days before the decision close.
title: Credit-spread changes lead Nasdaq-100 volatility (VXN)
